body.claimedTitle: The membership is on their own entry as memberOf, so there is nothing in the group to remove. An ldapmodify or a SCIM PATCH of the PERSON takes it away.
body.nobodyMatches: Nobody in the directory or among the people who have signed in matches that. To grant a role to a name this service has never seen, use the form below the results.
body.nobodyAtAll: Nobody is in the directory and nobody has signed in yet, so there is nobody to pick. The form below takes a typed name.
body.closed: Nobody can use this console. The gate is on, no role has a member, and {reason, select, claimed {the bootstrap administrator has already signed in. } product {this is product mode, which never opens the console to whoever signs in. } other {admin.openWhenEmpty is off. }}Anything you are reading here you are reading through /admin-api or with the gate off.
body.bootstrapPassword: Only {username}, signing in with its password, can use this console until it does. This is product mode and the console has not been claimed: the window in which anybody who signs in holds both roles is a development convenience and never opens here. Its first password sign-in through this realm claims the console; a sign-in as that account by any other method holds nothing until then. Anybody granted a role on this page holds it at once.
body.bootstrapUnclaimed: {username} has not signed in to this console yet, so anybody who signs in has the whole console. This service's bootstrap administrator holds both roles already; its first sign-in here ends the open console — for everybody who holds no role. Grant yourself a role now if you will need the console after that.
body.openToAnyone: No role has a member, so anybody who signs in has the whole console. The first grant made on this page ends that — for everybody, including whoever makes it. Grant yourself a role before you grant anybody else one, or the next page you click will be a 403.
body.enforced: The roster is enforced. {count} grant(s) across two roles; everybody else is refused at every page of this console.
body.notInForce: None of this is in force. The gate is OFF, so the console is open to anybody who can reach this port and these roles decide nothing. They are still real directory groups and can be granted now. (UNREACHABLE since 2026-09-06: the gate is unconditional.)
body.noDirectory: No LDAP directory is loaded in this process, so there is nowhere to hold these roles and nothing on this page can be granted. That is a build of this service without ldap_server.js rather than a failure — but the console gate is unconditional, so it leaves this console reachable only while admin.openWhenEmpty is on.
body.grantNote: Search for the person, then pick them from the results. The list is everybody with an entry in the directory and everybody this service has seen authenticate — two different sets, which is why both are searched and why each result says which it came from. An empty search lists everybody, twenty at a time.
body.typedHeading: Grant to a name that is not listed
body.name: Name
body.typedPlaceholder: the name they will sign in as
body.typedNote: The membership will DANGLE until that person exists — it names a DN this directory does not hold yet — and the role counts from the moment they first sign in. That is the interesting case for a mock and is why this form is here: nothing about a grant requires the person to have been seen. A name carrying a character RFC 4514 reserves in a DN is refused, the same refusal creating a person gets.
body.readOnlyNote: Granting and revoking need Admin Write. The table above is what you can see with Admin Read.
body.noMatch: No grant matches. The filter above may be hiding some.
body.whyOpen: Which is why anybody who signs in can read this page.
body.claimedNote: Some of those grants are on the PERSON rather than in the group. An entry whose own memberOf names a role group holds the role — the directory is asked in both directions — and nothing here maintains memberOf, so a client wrote it. They are listed because a page answering “who has access” that omitted them would be showing a console somebody could use and a list they were not on. They cannot be revoked from here: the value is on their entry, and this console writes only to groups. One edge worth knowing — a memberOf naming a role group that has never been created grants nothing, and starts granting the moment the first ordinary grant creates it.
body.notCreatedTitle: The group is created by the first grant rather than at startup, so "no group" and "no members" are the same state here.
body.claimedCountTitle: Of which {count} are claimed by the person's own memberOf rather than listed by the group.
body.writeImpliesRead: Write implies read. A member of {write} does not also need {read}: a role that could post a form to a page it was not allowed to look at would be a trap rather than a permission.
body.renaming: Renaming a role group does not move anybody. The members stay in the group they were put in, which stops granting anything the moment the name changes — and the new name grants nothing until somebody is put in it. /admin-api is not gated by any of these four, on purpose: it is the way back in when nobody who holds a role can sign in, and it is why turning the gate on does not break a test suite driving the management API.
rbacMemberCell.neverHereTitle: This person has an entry in the directory, but nothing here has authenticated as them yet, so there is no page about them on Users.
rbacMemberCell.danglingTitle: Nothing is at this DN. The role still counts — it resolves the moment somebody authenticates under this name or the entry is created — but until then no directory client can see who it names.
rbacClaimedMark.title: Their own entry's memberOf names this group and the group does not list them back. Nothing here maintains memberOf — a client wrote it — and it grants the role all the same, so it is on this list. The Revoke button cannot remove it: the value is on the person, and this console writes only to groups.
rbacCaveat.before: These two groups are the only groups in this service that grant anything, and what they grant is this console. Every other group here still grants nothing at all — see
rbacCaveat.after: , which says so — and even these two grant nothing outside /admin: no token's scopes change, no assertion gains an attribute, no Kerberos PAC is affected, and a member of admin-write gets exactly the same answer from /oauth2/token as anybody else. They are also ordinary directory entries, so ldapmodify, a SCIM PATCH, this page and POST /admin-api/rbac/grant are four doors onto one membership — which is the point rather than a leak: a role no test can grant is a role no test can exercise.
